data.name: Hareshwari
data.gender_notes: Hareshwari is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hareshwari is the name of the goddess who is considered the consort of Lord Vishnu. Her name is derived from 'Hara', meaning lord, and 'Ishwari', meaning goddess. Hareshwari is revered for her compassionate nature and her ability to protect her devotees from harm. The name Hareshwari carries the meaning “Goddess of Hari (Vishnu)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hareshwari usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of hari (vishnu) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hareshwari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Hari (Vishnu).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hareshwari total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Temples dedicated to Hareshwari can be found in various parts of India, and her festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm. historical_references.reference: Hareshwari is mentioned in the ancient Hindu scripture Mahabharata, as the name of the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha. She is also known as Subhadra, the sister of Arjuna.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an Indian epic that narrates the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes. Bhishma Pitamaha, an important character in the epic, is the grandsire of the Kurus and the grandfather of both the Pandavas and the Kauravas. Hareshwari is mentioned as his wife.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Hareshwari is found in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Harivamsa Purana, where she is described as the mother of Vidura, the advisor of the Kuru dynasty.
historical_references.context: The Harivamsa Purana is a Sanskrit Hindu scripture that is a part of the Mahapurana genre. The text is considered to be a continuation of the Mahabharata and provides additional details about the lives of various characters, including Vidura, who is a significant figure in the epic. Hareshwari is mentioned as his mother.
